questions.prompt: Which two cues support a wall-side hold?

options.text: Central lane is empty and open

questions.explanation: Middle is restricted and D2 is connected wall-side, so hold can preserve possession; an open middle is another picture.

questions.prompt: Arrange one change-management read.

options.text: Use D2 or wait until W is ready

questions.explanation: Pressure tells you where not to force; wall protection buys time; D2 or delayed release keeps change connected.

questions.prompt: Move D2 closer to YOU on the wall-side support lane.
questions.explanation: Closer wall support gives YOU a short connection while middle is covered; if Gold 1 follows, protect and wait.

questions.prompt: If middle opens before W returns, what can change?

options.text: Recheck whether a controlled middle connection helps
Leave puck because plan was wall-only

questions.explanation: The condition changed, so evaluate middle again; if Gold 1 closes it, return to wall protection.

questions.prompt: Why is a safe-side hold a decision rather than a default?
questions.explanation: It fits lead, change, pressure and D2 support, but a new lane or lost support changes the choice; puck and teammates still need reading.

after.title: Choose the safer side before a change

questions.prompt: What is the puck state?
questions.explanation: The puck marker is loose, so YOU reads a retrieval race while D1 protects inside; if control changes, roles update.

questions.prompt: Which two jobs need separating?
questions.explanation: The nearest player attacks puck while inside defender protects danger; two at wall exposes slot.

questions.prompt: Arrange one failed-clear recovery.

options.text: YOU retrieve if lane is reachable

questions.explanation: The call shares information; nearest route decides retrieval; D1’s inside position prevents free slot attack.

questions.prompt: Move D1 between Gold 1 and the Navy net while YOU attacks wall puck.
questions.explanation: D1’s net-side spot protects slot and leaves YOU retrieval lane; if Gold 1 wins puck, D1 becomes carrier defender.

questions.prompt: If Gold 1 gains clear control, what changes?

options.text: D1 contains new carrier while YOU recovers next inside lane
Both defenders remain tied to wall

questions.explanation: Clear control changes puck threat, so D1’s coverage and YOU’s recovery update; if Navy recovers, rebuild support.

questions.prompt: Why is a failed clear a role-change moment?
questions.explanation: The blocked puck removes assumption of exit, so one retrieves and another protects slot; if possession becomes clear, both jobs change.
